fullText.simplified:
第六章、我写《离骚》

    改革失败后，失望和难过把我打倒了。我离开引都，去了云梦泽。
    云梦泽是一个漂亮的地方，有山有水。我经常划着小船，在云梦泽的高山之间穿过。我看到山里的树叶在慢慢变黄，就像我的头发也在一点点变白。
    我还看到没有家的穷苦百姓就睡在路边，看到他们灰色的脸、瘦小的身体和破旧的衣服，我心痛极了。我把身上的钱分给他们，把自己的厚衣服送给他们。他们对我说着谢谢，这让我更心痛了。
    不管我在哪儿，不管我做什么，难过一直跟着我。希望国家变强，希望百姓的生活变好，希望楚怀王坚持理想，希望楚怀王再次信任我……这些声音每时每刻都在我的心里回响。
    没有人理解我的心，那就把它写进诗里吧！
    我又开始写诗了。我把我的难受、希望和理想全部写进了诗里。

    “时间过得太快，我跟不上，这太让人着急了。
    国家很强大，快点儿把那些不好的东西都改掉吧。
    ……
    我不担心自己，但我害怕国家走进危险里。
    我不害怕分开，但我担心你不能坚持理想。
    ……
    我为辛苦的百姓流泪，他们的生活多么困难！
    没有人理解我，而我又这么不愿意离开。
    ……”

    这首诗的名字叫《离骚》，它很长。后人说，他们喜欢《离骚》，他们在学校里学过这首诗。这是我没有想到的。写《离骚》的时候，我认为没有人会喜欢它，楚怀王应该也不喜欢。但我仍然希望楚怀王读到它，然后明白我、信任我、远离那些让他停止改革的人。
    当我在云梦泽难过时，引都发生了一些事情。
    听说，西边的秦国派了使者来引都。这位使者叫张宜。
fullText.traditional:
第六章、我寫《離騷》

    改革失敗後，失望和難過把我打倒了。我離開引都，去了雲夢澤。
    雲夢澤是一個漂亮的地方，有山有水。我經常划著小船，在雲夢澤的高山之間穿過。我看到山裡的樹葉在慢慢變黃，就像我的頭髮也在一點點變白。
    我還看到沒有家的窮苦百姓就睡在路邊，看到他們灰色的臉、瘦小的身體和破舊的衣服，我心痛極了。我把身上的錢分給他們，把自己的厚衣服送給他們。他們對我說著謝謝，這讓我更心痛了。
    不管我在哪兒，不管我做什麼，難過一直跟著我。希望國家變強，希望百姓的生活變好，希望楚懷王堅持理想，希望楚懷王再次信任我……這些聲音每時每刻都在我的心裡迴響。
    沒有人理解我的心，那就把它寫進詩裡吧！
    我又開始寫詩了。我把我的難受、希望和理想全部寫進了詩裡。

    “時間過得太快，我跟不上，這太讓人著急了。
    國家很強大，快點兒把那些不好的東西都改掉吧。
    ……
    我不擔心自己，但我害怕國家走進危險裡。
    我不害怕分開，但我擔心你不能堅持理想。
    ……
    我為辛苦的百姓流淚，他們的生活多麼困難！
    沒有人理解我，而我又這麼不願意離開。
    ……”

    這首詩的名字叫《離騷》，它很長。後人說，他們喜歡《離騷》，他們在學校裡學過這首詩。這是我沒有想到的。寫《離騷》的時候，我認為沒有人會喜歡它，楚懷王應該也不喜歡。但我仍然希望楚懷王讀到它，然後明白我、信任我、遠離那些讓他停止改革的人。
    當我在雲夢澤難過時，引都發生了一些事情。
    聽說，西邊的秦國派了使者來引都。這位使者叫張宜。

sentences.pinyin: méi yǒu rén lǐ jiě wǒ de xīn nà jiù bǎ tā xiě jìn shī lǐ ba
sentences.english: No one could understand my feelings, so I decided to write them into poetry!

sentences.traditional: 我又開始寫詩了。我把我的難受、希望和理想全部寫進了詩裡。

sentences.english: I started writing poetry again. I put all my sorrow, hopes, and ideals into my poems.

sentences.simplified: “时间过得太快，我跟不上，这太让人着急了。
sentences.traditional: “時間過得太快，我跟不上，這太讓人著急了。
sentences.pinyin: shí jiān guò de tài kuài wǒ gēn bú shàng zhè tài ràng rén zháo jí le
sentences.english: “Time passes too quickly. I can’t keep up, and it’s so frustrating.

sentences.simplified: 国家很强大，快点儿把那些不好的东西都改掉吧。
sentences.traditional: 國家很強大，快點兒把那些不好的東西都改掉吧。

sentences.simplified: 我不担心自己，但我害怕国家走进危险里。
sentences.traditional: 我不擔心自己，但我害怕國家走進危險裡。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ bù dān xīn zì jǐ dàn wǒ hài pà guó jiā zǒu jìn wēi xiǎn lǐ
sentences.english: I’m not worried about myself, but I’m afraid the country is moving toward danger.

sentences.simplified: 我不害怕分开，但我担心你不能坚持理想。
sentences.traditional: 我不害怕分開，但我擔心你不能堅持理想。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ bú hài pà fēn kāi dàn wǒ dān xīn nǐ bù néng jiān chí lǐ xiǎng
sentences.english: I’m not afraid of being apart, but I’m worried that you won’t be able to hold on to your ideals.

sentences.simplified: 我为辛苦的百姓流泪，他们的生活多么困难！
sentences.traditional: 我為辛苦的百姓流淚，他們的生活多麼困難！
sentences.pinyin: wǒ wèi xīn kǔ de bǎi xìng liú lèi tā men de shēng huó duō me kùn nan
sentences.english: I weep for the struggling people. Their lives are so hard!

sentences.simplified: 没有人理解我，而我又这么不愿意离开。
sentences.traditional: 沒有人理解我，而我又這麼不願意離開。
sentences.pinyin: méi yǒu rén lǐ jiě wǒ ér wǒ yòu zhè me bú yuàn yì lí kāi
sentences.english: No one understands me, and yet I am so unwilling to leave.

sentences.simplified: 这首诗的名字叫《离骚》，它很长。
sentences.traditional: 這首詩的名字叫《離騷》，它很長。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shǒu shī de míng zi jiào lí sāo tā hěn cháng
sentences.english: This poem is called “Sorrow at Parting”, and it is very long.

sentences.simplified: 后人说，他们喜欢《离骚》，他们在学校里学过这首诗。
sentences.traditional: 後人說，他們喜歡《離騷》，他們在學校裡學過這首詩。
sentences.pinyin: hòu rén shuō tā men xǐ huan lí sāo tā men zài xué xiào lǐ xué guò zhè shǒu shī
sentences.english: People of later generations said they loved “Sorrow at Parting”. They had studied the poem in school.

sentences.simplified: 这是我没有想到的。
sentences.traditional: 這是我沒有想到的。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shì wǒ méi yǒu xiǎng dào de
sentences.english: That was something I had never expected.

sentences.simplified: 写《离骚》的时候，我认为没有人会喜欢它，楚怀王应该也不喜欢。
sentences.traditional: 寫《離騷》的時候，我認為沒有人會喜歡它，楚懷王應該也不喜歡。
sentences.pinyin: xiě lí sāo de shí hou wǒ rèn wéi méi yǒu rén huì xǐ huan tā chǔ huái wáng yīng gāi yě bù xǐ huan
sentences.english: When I wrote “Sorrow at Parting”, I thought no one would like it, and that King Huai of Chu probably wouldn’t like it either.

sentences.simplified: 但我仍然希望楚怀王读到它，然后明白我、信任我、远离那些让他停止改革的人。
sentences.traditional: 但我仍然希望楚懷王讀到它，然後明白我、信任我、遠離那些讓他停止改革的人。
sentences.pinyin: dàn wǒ réng rán xī wàng chǔ huái wáng dú dào tā rán hòu míng bai wǒ xìn rèn wǒ yuǎn lí nà xiē ràng tā tíng zhǐ gǎi gé de rén
sentences.english: But I still hoped that King Huai of Chu would read it, understand me, trust me, and stay away from those who had made him stop the reforms.

sentences.simplified: 当我在云梦泽难过时，引都发生了一些事情。
sentences.traditional: 當我在雲夢澤難過時，引都發生了一些事情。

sentences.english: While I was in Yunmeng Lakes feeling sad, some things happened in Yindu.

sentences.simplified: 听说，西边的秦国派了使者来引都。这位使者叫张宜。
sentences.traditional: 聽說，西邊的秦國派了使者來引都。這位使者叫張宜。

sentences.english: I heard that the western state of Qin had sent an envoy to Yindu. This envoy was named Zhang Yi.

sentence_translations: Chapter 6: I Write Sorrow at Parting
After the failure of the reforms, disappointment and sadness overwhelmed me. I left Yindu and went to Yunmeng Lakes.
Yunmeng Lakes was a beautiful area with mountains and rivers. I often rowed a small boat through the high mountains of Yunmeng Lakes.
I saw the leaves in the mountains slowly turning yellow, just as my own hair was turning white, little by little.
I also saw destitute people with no homes sleeping by the roadside.
When I looked at their grey faces, thin bodies, and tattered clothes, my heart ached deeply.
I gave them the money I had and offered them my warm clothes. When they thanked me, it only made my heart ache even more.
No matter where I went or what I did, sorrow followed me everywhere.
I hoped the country would become strong, that the people’s lives would improve, ..
.. that King Huai of Chu would uphold his ideals, and that he would trust me again …
These voices constantly echoed through my heart.
No one could understand my feelings, so I decided to write them into poetry!
I started writing poetry again. I put all my sorrow, hopes, and ideals into my poems.
“Time passes too quickly. I can’t keep up, and it’s so frustrating.
The country is strong now. Hurry and get rid of all those bad things!
I’m not worried about myself, but I’m afraid the country is moving toward danger.
I’m not afraid of being apart, but I’m worried that you won’t be able to hold on to your ideals.
I weep for the struggling people. Their lives are so hard!
No one understands me, and yet I am so unwilling to leave.
This poem is called “Sorrow at Parting”, and it is very long.
People of later generations said they loved “Sorrow at Parting”. They had studied the poem in school.
That was something I had never expected.
When I wrote “Sorrow at Parting”, I thought no one would like it, and that King Huai of Chu probably wouldn’t like it either.
But I still hoped that King Huai of Chu would read it, understand me, trust me, and stay away from those who had made him stop the reforms.
While I was in Yunmeng Lakes feeling sad, some things happened in Yindu.
I heard that the western state of Qin had sent an envoy to Yindu. This envoy was named Zhang Yi.
